article_title: A Systematic Review of Automatic Question Generation for Educational Purposes
citation: Ghader Kurdi, Jared Leo, Bijan Parsia, Uli Sattler, Salam Al-Emari. (2020). A Systematic Review of Automatic Question Generation for Educational Purposes. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-019-00186-y
title: Two-dimensional classification of AQG methods by level of understanding and transformation procedure
description: The review proposes a new classification of question generation approaches along two dimensions the authors say existing schemes miss: "the level of understanding of the input required by the generation approach" and "the procedure for transforming the input into questions". Level of understanding divides into syntactic and semantic approaches; transformation procedure divides into template, rule, and statistical methods. The categories are explicitly not mutually exclusive, and the classification extends and re-organises the scheme of Yao et al. (2012) as extended by Alsubait (2015).
requirements: Knowledge of the input representation (syntactic features, semantic relations, or training data) appropriate to the chosen category
constraints: The authors state the categories are not mutually exclusive
The authors regard Alsubait's template/schema distinction as unclear and collapse it into template-based
target_learners: developers and researchers of educational question generation systems
target_learning_goals: automatic production of assessment and practice questions
examples: Gao et al. (2018) treated question generation as a sequence-to-sequence prediction problem learned from training data
Mazidi and Tarau (2016a, b) matched the pattern "S-V-acomp" to the template "Indicate properties or characteristics of S?"
key_sources: Ghader Kurdi, Jared Leo, Bijan Parsia, Uli Sattler, Salam Al-Emari. (2020). A Systematic Review of Automatic Question Generation for Educational Purposes. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-019-00186-y

article_title: Analysis of swimming teaching programs, aquatic competencies and specific skills in school settings from early childhood to secondary education: A systematic review.
citation: Trinidad Alfonso, Mendoza-Castejón Daniel, Mercedes de la Calle Laura, del-Blanco-Muñiz José Ángel. (2026). Analysis of swimming teaching programs, aquatic competencies and specific skills in school settings from early childhood to secondary education: A systematic review. PLOS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0353477
title: Aquatic competence and aquatic literacy as a comprehensive competency framework for school swimming
description: The review organises its analysis around the concepts of aquatic competence and aquatic literacy, defined as "the integration of the knowledge, skills, attitudes and behaviours necessary to interact safely and competently in aquatic environments". Aquatic competence is described as "the multidimensional set of motor skills, safety knowledge and self-assessment abilities that enable a person to interact effectively and safely with the aquatic environment". The framework represents a paradigm shift from isolated techniques and strokes toward integrating physical, cognitive and affective competencies, aligned with the European ALFAC project.
requirements: Teaching must go beyond knowing how to swim, integrating safety knowledge, self-assessment abilities and attitudes alongside motor skills
constraints: The review notes swimming skills alone are not sufficient to prevent drowning
target_learners: school-aged children from early childhood to secondary education
examples: The review used a technical-functional versus educational-curricular coding rubric to classify the 16 studies against this framework

article_title: Face and content validation of a novel aquablation training simulator: an educational project of the European school of urology.
citation: Demirkıran Engin Denizhan, Şener Tarık Emre, Perri Davide, de Oliveira Tiago Ribeiro, Caballero Juan Pablo, Osorio Luis, Kartalas Ioannis Goumas, Ramos Rodrigo, Castro Afonso Sousa, Reis Daniel Oliveira, Pereira Sergio, Dragos Laurian, Veneziano Domenico, Bozzini Giorgio, Somani Bhaskar, Liatsikos Evangelos. (2026). Face and content validation of a novel aquablation training simulator: an educational project of the European school of urology. Journal of Robotic Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11701-026-03388-4
title: Aquablation training simulator integrating prostate phantom, TRUS-based guidance, and waterjet ablation interface
description: A physical training station combining the AquaBeam® Robotic System, an EndoUroPhantom training box, and 3D-printed prostate phantoms derived from patient imaging of a representative 60 cc prostate made of "soft, non-toxic biomimetic hydrogel materials". It integrates three components: anatomical representation of prostate, bladder neck and urethral landmarks; an "Ultrasound-based guidance system, replicating transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) views"; and a software and waterjet ablation interface simulating probe placement, contour definition, and real-time ablation with visual feedback of tissue clearance. It was evaluated at EUREP 2025 by expert endourologists.
requirements: Requires the AquaBeam® Robotic System, EndoUroPhantom training box, and 3D-printed prostate phantoms by Quantitative Surgical GmbH as printed in the article
constraints: The model does not reproduce bleeding control or fully realistic tissue behavior, as its primary purpose is to simulate the planning and robotic Aquablation phase rather than the subsequent endoscopic hemostatic step
target_learners: Urology residents and trainees in lower urinary tract endoscopy
target_learning_goals: Fundamental technical aspects of Aquablation, including TRUS-guided mapping, contouring, probe alignment, and waterjet ablation planning
examples: Assessed by twelve expert urologists during a structured training session at EUREP 2025 in Prague following a demonstration and hands-on experience

article_title: Face and content validation of a novel aquablation training simulator: an educational project of the European school of urology.
citation: Demirkıran Engin Denizhan, Şener Tarık Emre, Perri Davide, de Oliveira Tiago Ribeiro, Caballero Juan Pablo, Osorio Luis, Kartalas Ioannis Goumas, Ramos Rodrigo, Castro Afonso Sousa, Reis Daniel Oliveira, Pereira Sergio, Dragos Laurian, Veneziano Domenico, Bozzini Giorgio, Somani Bhaskar, Liatsikos Evangelos. (2026). Face and content validation of a novel aquablation training simulator: an educational project of the European school of urology. Journal of Robotic Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11701-026-03388-4
title: Six-domain task deconstruction of the Aquablation workflow as the basis for validation questionnaires
description: Before creating the survey, faculty experienced in Aquablation deconstructed the procedure into a pragmatic task structure organized into six domains: "(1) prostate mapping with TRUS, (2) contour definition, (3) probe alignment, (4) waterjet ablation, (5) identification of procedural endpoints, and (6) basic troubleshooting". This domain structure generated the item pool for the face and content validity questionnaires and provides a framework for the planned CTA and Delphi-based consensus steps. The authors stress it was not a formal CTA and did not define a complete curriculum or proficiency benchmarks.
requirements: Deconstruction by faculty experienced in Aquablation and endourological training; the authors state a formal CTA and Delphi process are still needed for curriculum specification
constraints: This process was not a formal CTA and was not intended to define a complete ESU curriculum or proficiency benchmarks
target_learners: Urology residents in European Urology Residents Education Programme settings
target_learning_goals: Structured acquisition of the core Aquablation procedural workflow
examples: The domain structure generated the initial item pool for the 11-item face and 12-item content questionnaires used at EUREP 2025
